ios.desc:
Some thoughts take shape out loud: an idea on a walk, a worry after a conversation, a decision you need to hear yourself make.

Sanctum is a voice journal for thoughts that are still in process. Start before you know exactly where the thought is going. Ramble, correct yourself, and change your mind. Sanctum keeps the original and turns the whole train of thought into a clear note you can return to.

 Sanctum never uses your recordings, transcripts, notes or any of your data for tracking, advertising, analytics, or AI training.

FIND THE THREAD

• Turn one recording—or a thought captured in pieces—into a clear, grounded note
• Surface useful patterns, tensions, insights, and questions to carry forward
• Keep adding recordings as an idea changes
• Search by meaning, even when you no longer remember the words you used
• Let Echoes bring back one exact line from your own past notes

KEEP THE WHOLE THOUGHT

Every note keeps its source close: the audio, structured transcript, synthesis, and one readable combined document. Listen again, check the writing against what you actually said, rename and edit the result, or share it when you are ready.

CAPTURE WHILE IT IS MOVING

Record with one tap in the app. On supported iPhone models, put Sanctum on the Action Button to begin with one press and save with another. Pause, resume, organize notes into enclaves, folders, and tags, and restore deleted work from Trash.

YOUR NOTE, IN FILES YOU OWN

Each note is an ordinary folder on your device. Open it in the Files app, copy it, back it up, or take the Markdown somewhere else. Your files remain readable outside Sanctum.

CLEAR CHOICES ABOUT PROCESSING

No account is required to record, store, play, browse, search, organize, edit, rename, share, or export your notes. On supported devices and languages, transcription can happen on device.

Sign-in is required only for optional work that leaves the device and incurs processing costs: server-side transcription and synthesis, and Private Backup. Sanctum shows the processing choice before you record.

You can try server analysis before creating an account. New accounts include complimentary server-analysis minutes. Additional minutes are available through monthly subscriptions or a one-time top-up. Recording, playback, file ownership, on-device transcription, search, editing, and sharing remain free.

Terms of Use (EULA): https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/itunes/dev/stdeula/
Privacy Policy: https://speakwithsanctum.

quotes.text:
Greetings friends!  I have been joyfully working on a native iOS app called Sanctum.  I really built this for myself and use it multiple times a day (https://apps.apple.com/us/app/sanctum-the-voice-journal/id6796428879)

Sanctum is a voice journal, think Obsidian but for voice notes.  I am really honing in on data sovereignty, privacy, 1 click to record and self organization of notes / ideas.

While this isn't anything revolutionary, or technically difficult, I do think I've landed on a form factor and stack that is in my opinion not served by current products.  So much so that I just simply had to build it myself. Sanctum was born out of an Obsidian plugin that I built and have been maintaining for about 2 years called Scribe and it's been a wonderful way to really hone in on a more full fledged agentic development process for a full stack experience.

The stack is simple

  - For transcription I am using AssemblyAI - they have solid terms, 24hr retention and no training

  - LLM inference is running inside a TEE using redpill.ai, it's slow af but as private as I could find.

  - For cloud backup I am using full E2E encryption with Backblaze for storage

  - Endpoints and the like are AWS lambdas, DynamoDB for billing storage, Supabase for auth

I (yes, fully me, not AI) have been doing a lot of writing on the process, we are flooded with these sorts of post on HN, but if anyone is interested in reading, check it out! …
quotes.story_title: Ask HN: What are you working on? (September 2026)
